Threat.value: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: For a police-related trauma, the combination of threat items is not fully coherent: startle response and physical reactivity fit PTSD, but risky behavior is a different symptom style and is weakly connected to the rest of this profile. With only Threat and Memory represented, risky behavior lacks support from the other selected items and does not read as a clear trauma-linked threat perception.

issues.item: Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
issues.explanation: Within Memory, the items suggest overwhelmed, poorly verbalized traumatic recall, which is coherent for PTSD. However, intense guilt on recall introduces a strong negative appraisal theme that is otherwise absent from the profile. Given the formulation only shows a Threat → Memory link and no active Negative Appraisals connections, this item is not well aligned with the stated cognitive pattern.

vignette: Kofi's eyes still widened when he recalled the night he was stopped by police on his way home from a late meeting with colleagues. It had been a routine traffic stop, but the officer's tone and mannerisms had escalated the situation, leaving Kofi shaken. The memory of being ordered out of his car, hands raised, while his wife watched from the passenger seat, still felt like an open wound. When it resurfaced, as it often did in the months that followed, Kofi felt overwhelmed by a mix of emotions: fear, anger, and helplessness. He would have to stop whatever he was doing - whether working on a curriculum design project or helping his kids with homework - and collect himself before he could continue. As time passed, Kofi found it increasingly difficult to articulate what had happened that night. The details seemed to slip away from him like sand between his fingers. When he tried to recount the events to friends or family, he would become frustrated by his inability to put the experience into words. His wife, Nana, would often finish his sentences for him, as if trying to fill in the gaps. But even with her support, Kofi felt like a part of him was frozen in time. Physical reactions became more common, too. When he heard sirens or saw police cars on the road, his heart rate would spike, and his palms would grow sweaty. He began to notice how jumpy he had become - how easily startled by sudden noises or movements. His kids would tease him about being "on edge" all the time, but Kofi knew it wasn't just a joke. He felt like he was constantly on guard, waiting for something else to go wrong. As a curriculum designer, Kofi's work required him to be creative and focused. But since the incident, he had found himself increasingly preoccupied with thoughts of safety and security. He would get caught up in hypothetical scenarios - what if this happened, or that? - and before long, his mind would wander back to that fateful night. His colleagues began to notice a change in him; meetings would pass without Kofi contributing much, as he was lost in thought. Nana noticed the changes too, of course. She would try to reassure him, reminding him that they were safe now, but Kofi couldn't shake off the feeling of vulnerability. At times, he felt like he was drowning in emotions without being able to recall the exact events that had triggered them. His family life began to suffer as a result; dinner conversations grew strained, and plans for weekend outings were cancelled due to Kofi's anxiety. One evening, as they sat down for dinner, their daughter asked why Dad seemed so "sad" all the time. Nana tried to explain, but Kofi knew he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this - constantly on edge, unable to shake off the memories of that night. The realization hit him: it was time to seek professional help, not just for himself, but for his family's sake as well.
